name: Commodity basis-momentum

how_it_works.simple: Compare how much the nearest oil or gas contract has gained over the past year with the next contract out. If the near one has gained more, buy; if less, sell.
how_it_works.analogy: Like noticing that this week's concert tickets are selling faster than next month's: the pressure is at the front, and it tends to keep pushing.
how_it_works.precise: Basis-momentum is the 12-month cumulative return of a first-nearby futures position minus that of a second-nearby position. Sorting 21 commodities on it (top four minus bottom four) earned 18.38% a year, Sharpe 0.92, over 1960-08 to 2014-02; the calendar-spread version (nearby minus second-nearby returns) earned 4.08% a year, Sharpe 0.88, and 1.06 after 1986.

rule: Monthly, per energy contract: BM = prod(1 + r_C1 over 12 months) - prod(1 + r_C2 over 12 months). Time-series version: long the rolled future if BM > 0, short if BM < 0, inverse volatility weights. Spread version: long contract 1 and short contract 2 when BM > 0, the reverse when BM < 0.
data_needed: Daily NYMEX contract 1 and 2 prices (EIA, to April 2024)
economic_rationale: Maturity-specific price pressure that builds when rising volatility limits speculators' capacity to take the other side of hedgers; distinct from storage, inventories and hedging pressure according to the authors.
why_it_might_fail: Our version has four correlated energy contracts, not 21; the per-commodity time-series and spread versions are our adaptation; spread returns are small, so costs bite.

reported_results.source: Boons and Prado (2019), working paper, Table 1 Panel A, High4-minus-Low4 nearby returns
reported_results.notes: Sample from 1986-02 to 2014-02: 16.77% a year, Sharpe 0.80. Basis alone -10.61% (Sharpe -0.53), momentum alone 15.02% (Sharpe 0.63) over the full sample.

reported_results.source: Boons and Prado (2019), working paper, Table 1 Panel B, High4-minus-Low4 spreading returns
reported_results.notes: Full sample 1960-08 to 2014-02: 4.08% a year, Sharpe 0.88.

post_publication_evidence: Kwon, Kang and Yun (2021, Finance Research Letters) split the ranking period and find its parts behave differently; we found no test on data after February 2014.

relevance.reason: Strongest commodity signal we found, and our EIA data from 2014-03 to 2024-04 lies entirely after the paper's sample.
